description:
11034 pre/post-disaster WorldView pairs of 1024x1024 over 19 events, every building outlined and graded on the release's four-level damage scale plus an `un-classified` grade that is the ignore index. Six hazard types: fire, flooding, wind, earthquake, tsunami and volcano.

**Targets.** Outlines come from the post label, where the grade lives, as flat pixel rings with a per-object vertex count. The release's WGS84 ring is preserved beside them because the PNGs carry no geotransform.

**Capture geometry.** Kept per sample for both halves -- sensor, GSD, off-nadir angle, sun elevation -- since the two passes differ and that difference is a confound.

**Splits.**
- tier-3 is more training data rather than a third split, and is marked `release_tier` (train 2799, tier3 6369, hold 933, test 933).
- `hold` is the challenge holdout, fetched separately from a signed-in xview2.org session and labelled like train and tier3, so it is carried here as this container's `test`, with the archive name in `split_original`.
- `val` is carved from train + tier3 on whole events.
- The challenge's unlabelled half is `xview2_test`.

**Scope.** xBD's whole named release. The only pairs not here are the 933 of the anonymised test archive, which carry no disaster and no scene id. PNGs are stored byte-for-byte.

ml:polygon_xy.description: Building outlines, FLAT: every vertex of every building end to end as x, y pixel pairs

ml:post_gsd_m.description: Ground sample distance of the post image, metres

ml:post_off_nadir_deg.description: Off-nadir angle of the post pass

ml:post_sun_azimuth_deg.description: Sun azimuth at the post pass

ml:post_sun_elevation_deg.description: Sun elevation at the post pass

ml:pre_gsd_m.description: Ground sample distance of the pre image, metres

ml:pre_off_nadir_deg.description: Off-nadir angle of the pre pass

ml:pre_sun_azimuth_deg.description: Sun azimuth at the pre pass

ml:pre_sun_elevation_deg.description: Sun elevation at the pre pass

ml:release_tier.description: Which release archive the pair came from: train or tier3. Both are training data
